metadata.verification_method: CoVe Factored Verification with 3/5 Majority Rule
metadata.graph_description: Verified attack graph for Kaseya Unitrends Backup vulnerabilities centered on CVE-2017-12477, containing only evidence-based relationships that passed both frequency (≥3/5) and factual verification checks.

nodes.description: Authentication bypass in bpserverd proprietary protocol leading to remote code execution with root privileges
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Remote Code Execution
nodes.precondition: network access to bpserverd service through xinetd
nodes.postcondition: arbitrary command execution with root privileges

nodes.description: Input validation bypass in api/storage web interface leading to authentication bypass and remote code execution with root privileges
nodes.vulnerability_type: Input Validation Bypass leading to Authentication Bypass and RCE
nodes.precondition: network access to api/storage web interface
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary commands executed with root privileges

nodes.description: Authentication bypass in user interface allowing unauthenticated command injection via /api/hosts parameters
nodes.vulnerability_type: Authentication Bypass leading to Command Injection
nodes.precondition: network access to user interface /api/hosts endpoint
nodes.postcondition: authentication bypassed and arbitrary command injection via backquotes

nodes.description: Privilege escalation vulnerability allowing read-only users to gain administrative privileges
Authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in server software
Remote code execution via command injection in bpserverd daemon, exploiting untrusted input passed to system calls
nodes.vulnerability_type: Remote Code Execution via Command Injection
nodes.precondition: ability to send untrusted input to bpserverd daemon

nodes.description: Local privilege escalation via world writable file allowing code execution as apache user
nodes.vulnerability_type: Local Privilege Escalation via Insecure File Permissions

nodes.description: Weak default password for PostgreSQL wguest account enabling unauthorized database access
nodes.precondition: knowledge of weak password or brute force capability

nodes.description: Privilege escalation from wguest to postgres user via PostgreSQL trigger function injection
nodes.vulnerability_type: Privilege Escalation via SQL Trigger Injection
nodes.postcondition: postgres user privileges obtained via trigger function injection

nodes.description: Anonymous read/write access to Samba file sharing service due to improper access control
nodes.postcondition: anonymous read/write access to file shares

nodes.description: Arbitrary file write vulnerability in privileged vaultServer component leading to privilege escalation
nodes.vulnerability_type: Arbitrary File Write leading to Privilege Escalation
nodes.precondition: ability to interact with privileged vaultServer
nodes.postcondition: arbitrary file creation and privilege escalation

nodes.description: Format string vulnerability in privileged vaultServer application exploitable via crafted HTTP requests
nodes.precondition: ability to send crafted HTTP requests to vaultServer
nodes.postcondition: potential code execution in privileged vaultServer context

nodes.description: Unauthenticated remote buffer overflow in vaultServer component exploitable by remote attackers
Arbitrary file read vulnerability via insecure Sudo rule allowing apache user to access sensitive files
nodes.vulnerability_type: Arbitrary File Read via Sudo Misconfiguration
nodes.postcondition: ability to read sensitive files including /etc/shadow

links.description: Both vulnerabilities exploit authentication bypass in Unitrends Backup versions before 10.0.0 to achieve remote code execution with root privileges. CVE-2017-12477 targets the bpserverd daemon while CVE-2017-12478 targets the api/storage web interface, demonstrating parallel attack vectors with identical outcomes.
links.evidence: Same version range (< 10.0.0), same vulnerability class (authentication bypass), same postcondition (root RCE), different attack surfaces (bpserverd vs api/storage)

links.description: Both vulnerabilities exploit the bpserverd daemon to achieve arbitrary remote code execution as root. CVE-2017-12477 uses authentication bypass while CVE-2021-43033 uses command injection via untrusted input, targeting the same critical component across different version ranges.
links.evidence: Same target component (bpserverd daemon), same postcondition (root RCE), similar exploitation methodology

links.description: CVE-2018-6328 represents an incomplete fix of CVE-2017-12478. While CVE-2017-12478 was patched in version 10.0.0, authentication bypass vulnerabilities persisted in versions before 10.1.0 (CVE-2018-6328), indicating the original patch did not comprehensively address the underlying authentication mechanism flaws.
links.evidence: Temporal sequence (2017 -> 2018), overlapping version ranges (< 10.0.0 -> < 10.1.0), persistent vulnerability type (authentication bypass leading to command execution)

links.description: CVE-2021-40385's privilege escalation from read-only to admin directly satisfies the authentication precondition required for CVE-2021-40387's authenticated remote code execution. Admin privileges provide the necessary authentication context for exploiting CVE-2021-40387.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-40385 postcondition (Admin privileges obtained) matches CVE-2021-40387 precondition (User authentication), both affecting same version range (< 10.5.5-2)

links.description: Reciprocal relationship to link 2. Both vulnerabilities target the bpserverd daemon for root-level remote code execution, representing persistent security weaknesses in this critical component across multiple Unitrends Backup versions.
links.evidence: Same target component (bpserverd), same postcondition (root RCE), different exploitation techniques across version ranges

links.description: CVE-2021-43034's successful exploitation grants apache user privileges, which directly satisfies the precondition for CVE-2021-43043. Once apache user access is obtained, the insecure Sudo rule can be abused to read arbitrary files including /etc/shadow.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43034 postcondition (apache user access) exactly matches CVE-2021-43043 precondition (apache user access), same version range (< 10.5.5)

links.description: CVE-2021-43036's weak wguest account password provides the exact access required to exploit CVE-2021-43038. Once wguest account access is obtained through the weak password, an attacker can inject malicious PostgreSQL trigger functions to escalate privileges to the postgres user.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43036 postcondition (wguest PostgreSQL account access) exactly matches CVE-2021-43038 precondition (wguest PostgreSQL account access), same platform (PostgreSQL), same version range (< 10.5.5)

links.description: CVE-2021-43039's anonymous Samba write access enables attackers to modify the world writable file exploited in CVE-2021-43034. The Samba service's read/write permissions provide the file system access necessary to manipulate files and trigger the privilege escalation vulnerability.
links.evidence: CVE-2021-43039 postcondition (anonymous write access) enables manipulation of world writable files exploited in CVE-2021-43034, same version range (< 10.5.5)

links.description: Both vulnerabilities target the privileged vaultServer component using different exploitation techniques. CVE-2021-43040 uses arbitrary file write while CVE-2021-43041 uses format string injection, representing multiple attack vectors against the same critical component.
links.evidence: Same target component (vaultServer), same version range (< 10.5.5), similar exploitation methodology targeting privileged service

links.description: Both vulnerabilities are memory corruption flaws in the vaultServer component. CVE-2021-43041 exploits a format string vulnerability while CVE-2021-43042 exploits a buffer overflow, representing the same vulnerability class (memory corruption) in the same component with different triggers.
links.evidence: Same target component (vaultServer), same vulnerability class (memory corruption), same version range (< 10.5.5), different exploitation techniques (format string vs buffer overflow)
